docs.title: Manage Warehouse Transfers, Lots, Short Receipts, and Replenishment

sections.text: This guide walks warehouse operators through daily inventory tasks in ERPForAll. You will learn how to navigate the Inventory Overview, review lot information, process a vendor receipt when fewer items arrive than scheduled, generate a manual replenishment quotation under the Buy route, and confirm the resulting stock position on the stock report.

Before performing these procedures, ensure you have access to the **Inventory** app and the appropriate operational permissions: * **Role & Access**: You must be an inventory operator or stock user authorized for the active company. To view lot registers, your user account requires the **Lot and serial tracking** group assigned under **Access Rights → Groups** by an administrator. For replenishment requests, the **Purchase Stock** addon must be installed, and your account must have permissions to update reordering rules and create purchase orders. * **Warehouse Setup**: Ensure a warehouse is configured with direct receiving into stock and that operation types (such as Receiving) have a designated sequence prefix. * **Master Data**: The product must exist in the inventory catalog. Lot tracking is optional: a product can be tracked by lot, by serial number, or not at all (units in stock without lots are tracked without numbers). If replenishment is triggered, the product requires a configured vendor with a current vendor price that covers the requested purchase quantity.

Follow these steps to find an incoming receipt and inspect lot traceability details: 1. Open **Inventory** to view the **Overview** dashboard. Cards display active operation types with counts for **To Process**, **Waiting**, **Late**, and **Backorders**. 2. Locate the card for your warehouse's receipt operation type (such as **Receiving**) and click the **To Process** count to view ready transfers, or navigate to **Operations → Receipts**. 3. In the transfer list, review the reference number, source and destination locations, partner contact, scheduled date, source document, and status. Click an open receipt in **Ready** status to open its transfer form. 4. Review the header details and select the **Operations** tab to see product lines, initial demand, and units. Switch to the **Detailed Operations** tab to view the move lines where lot allocations are tracked. 5. To independently verify registered lots across locations, open **Inventory → Products → Lots/Serial Numbers** (or **Inventory → Configuration → Settings**, then **Traceability → Lots and serial numbers**). Click a specific lot record to review its assigned product and location history. ![The Inventory overview groups work by operation type.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IndoERP/ERPForAll/a0b166f13a9bfef45efe154016c4f5d9fd2e37c0/.github/assets/inventory-overview.png)

When a shipment arrives with fewer items than ordered, record the actual delivered quantity and post the transfer: 1. On the open receipt form, switch to the **Detailed Operations** tab. 2. Locate the product line being received and adjust the **Done** (or quantity moved) field to match the quantity physically delivered instead of the full planned demand (for example, entering 8 units when the demand was 10 units). 3. Click **Validate** at the top of the transfer form. 4. Depending on the operation type's **Create Backorder** configuration: * If set to **Always**: The transfer finishes the entered quantity and automatically generates a new, numbered backorder transfer for the remaining balance. The new transfer's **Back Order of** field references the original receipt. * If set to **Ask**: A prompt displays the outstanding quantities. Click **Create Backorder** to schedule the remaining balance on a linked transfer, or **Close Remaining Demand** to cancel the balance. * If set to **Never**: The transfer closes immediately at the received quantity with no backorder. 5. Click **Create Backorder** if prompted. The original transfer status changes from **Ready** to **Done**, moving the received stock into your destination warehouse location.

When inventory drops below desired safety levels, warehouse operators can generate a draft request for quotation using an established reordering rule: 1. Navigate to **Inventory → Configuration → Replenishment** (or **Inventory → Configuration → Settings → Planning → Reordering rules (minimum and maximum)**). 2. Open the reordering rule for the product. Verify that the route is set to **Buy** and the destination points to your direct-receiving warehouse stock location. 3. Verify the **Min Quantity** and **Max Quantity** thresholds in the product's inventory unit, and ensure the product has a valid vendor price covering the purchase volume. 4. Click **Request Quotation**. 5. The system computes the forecasted stock (combining current on-hand quantities with scheduled incoming receipts and outgoing deliveries): * **Replenishment Example**: With min 3, max 6, and a forecasted stock of 2, clicking **Request Quotation** creates a draft RFQ for 4 units to bring stock up to the maximum target of 6. If a positive manual quantity is entered on the rule, that manual override takes precedence. * **Above Threshold**: If forecasted stock is 5 (at or above the minimum of 3), no RFQ is generated without a positive manual override, and the system explains why the rule requires no quotation. * **Pending Request Idempotency**: Opening or clicking **Request Quotation** on an existing pending request twice returns the same draft quotation rather than duplicating orders.

If an operation fails during validation or replenishment, identify the cause and recover using these verified steps: * **Negative Stock Refusal on Validation**: If an operation or transfer attempts to move or reserve items from a storage location that forbids negative stock and insufficient free stock exists, the system refuses **Validate** and displays an error naming the location and the free available quantity. No stock moves, and the transfer remains in its previous open state. * *Recovery*: Switch to **Detailed Operations** and correct the quantity to not exceed the available free stock, or wait until prior receipts are validated to replenish the location before clicking **Validate** again. * **Replenishment Quotation Not Needed**: If you click **Request Quotation** when the product's forecasted quantity is already equal to or greater than the defined minimum, the system displays an explanatory message indicating why no quotation was generated. * *Recovery*: Check **Inventory → Reporting → Product Stock Position** to review current reservations and open incoming orders before modifying threshold parameters on the reordering rule.

Confirm that stock ledger entries and physical counts match what was processed: 1. Navigate to **Inventory → Reporting → Stock**. 2. Locate the row corresponding to your received product, warehouse location, and lot number. 3. Open the line to view the read-only stock record. Verify that **On Hand** has incremented by the exact quantity received, **Reserved** reflects any existing outbound reservations, and **Available** displays the unreserved balance. 4. For comprehensive tracking across warehouse zones, navigate to **Inventory → Reporting → Stock Report**, expand the destination location, and expand the product to verify lot-level quantities. 5. To verify inventory movements over time, open **Inventory → Reporting → Moves Analysis** to confirm that the completed incoming transfer appears under **Incoming** with matching demand and delivered quantities.

In Inventory, open the supplier receipt and check the company, destination and received quantities. When Stock Valuation Admission is installed, a stock manager validates receipts of company-owned storable products into an internal or transit location of the same company. Select the receipt's company among your active companies. Validation records the physical receipt and reserves its company/product control for the transaction. The control carries no price.

For an access refusal, ask a stock manager with access to the company and the transfer to validate it. If a valuation seal or a competing operation prevents completion, refresh the transfer and check its state before retrying. A seal that continues to block receipts needs administrator attention. If an integration submits several pickings in one transaction, send the full batch in one validation so the system can reserve every affected product before moving stock. If validation reports too many receipt sources, split the receipt batch into smaller operations. Repeated lines for the same product also count toward this limit. An administrator can adjust the bounded source-row limit in Technical System Parameters.
